title: Enfusion workspace
description: The optional file a monorepo of mods puts above them. It says nothing about any one mod: what it holds is the launch block, and it holds it for every mod under it. A single mod does without this file. The launch block is spelled out here rather than referenced from mod.enf.schema.json, because a relative $ref between two schema files of an extension does not resolve: the editor loses the base URI and goes looking for file:///./<name>. schemas.test.ts keeps the copy in step.

$schema.description: The schema this file is written against, for an editor that finds it that way rather than by the file name.

launch.description: How the mods of this workspace are launched. This block wins whole: the one in a mod.enf under it is ignored rather than merged.
Everything about getting the game up: where the built mods are, which third-party mods join them, and what the Run and Debug list offers.

modsDirectory.description: Where the @<Mod> folders live: the builder writes them here, and the game is pointed at them here. A relative path is counted from the folder this file is in, which is what keeps it meaning the same thing on every machine that clones the repository.

clientMods.description: Every mod the client loads, in load order, by the name of its folder in modsDirectory, with or without the leading @. Handed to the client alone as -mod=; the server reads none of it. Mods of this workspace are not added on their own: one is loaded because it is named here, the same as any other, so a mod the workspace holds and no launch wants is left out.

serverMods.description: Every mod the server loads, in load order, named the same way. Handed to the server alone as -serverMod=; the client reads none of it. The two lists are independent — a mod both sides need has to be named in both — and mods of this workspace are not added on their own here either.

targets.description: The entries of the Run and Debug list. Each one says what to put up and where its profile and mission come from.

name.description: What the Run and Debug list shows this target as.

mod.description: The mod the profile, the mission and the server.cfg come from. The mod being launched when left out.

map.description: The world this target is about, which is the tail of the mission folder name — sakhal, chernarusplus. A server loads the mission the target's mod keeps for it, Missions\<Mod>.<map>, with the Global and Dev layers of Missions laid over it; a client with no server to join loads dayzOffline.<map> instead.

enumDescriptions: The server, and a client that joins it.

serverConfig.description: The server.cfg the dev server is started with, relative to the target's mod. Left out, the mod's own server.cfg is used, and failing that the one beside the file that owns this launch block.
